channel.title: Global Competition Review - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Global Competition Review (globalcompetitionreview.com)

item.title: Live Nation trial to test DOJ’s jury strategy
item.description: The Department of Justice’s monopolisation suit against Live Nation may be the first civil case the Antitrust Division has ever tried before a jury, serving as a potential bellwether for future Section 2 cases.

item.title: DOJ rebukes information exchange defence
item.description: The Department of Justice has rebuffed claims made by producers of frozen potato products that reciprocal information exchanges are “insufficient” to establish concerted action.

item.title: Unhappy hour: The Briefing for 3 March 2026
item.description: Heineken will have to pick up the tab for at least €43 million in damages suffered by Greek brewer Macedonian Thrace Brewery, after a Dutch district court published an interim judgment on Friday quantifying the amount owed. The Greek brewer claims this figure will rise to at least €83 million when interest is added, though Heineken maintains that the lawsuit is “without merit”. Also in The Briefin...

item.title: “Friends” and “foes”: The Tipline for 3 March 2026
item.description: Money will not make antitrust crimes disappear, according to the Department of Justice’s antitrust division. Acting Assistant Attorney General Omeed Assefi said at GCR Live: Cartels on Tuesday that the Antitrust Division is “not looking for settlement cheques” but “prison sentences”. item.title: US pushes Indonesia to screen foreign investments in ‘reciprocal’ trade deal
item.description: The US government has instructed Indonesia to “establish and apply” its own inbound investment screening framework as part of its latest tariffs deal with a Southeast Asian country.

item.title: Boswell joins Norton Rose Fulbright in Canada
item.description: Norton Rose Fulbright has added the former head of Canada’s Competition Bureau to its ranks as a partner in Ottawa.

item.title: Chile’s top court strikes out interlocking directorate sanctions
item.description: Chile’s Supreme Court has overturned several fines against companies punished for violating the country’s interlocking directorate rules, ruling that businesses can only be sanctioned if they directly compete against each other and any anticompetitive effects are properly evidenced.

item.title: Merricks will not replace deceased class representative in UK claim
item.description: Walter Merricks has opted not to apply to become the class representative in a collective action against Govia Thameslink Railway after failing to secure the necessary insurance.

item.title: Live Nation doc described “robbing” concertgoers, DOJ says
item.description: Internal records reveal Live Nation knew it was exploiting its monopoly to “rob [concertgoers] blind,” the Department of Justice said Tuesday as it opened its watershed bid to break up the world’s biggest concert promoter.

item.title: DOJ’s Glad downplays “trial risk” with whistleblowers
item.description: The Department of Justice’s top official for criminal antitrust matters has rejected criticism that juries will not trust trial testimony from witnesses that stand to gain financial awards for their cooperation.
